name: Nasirul Mulk
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; qualified as a barrister at age 26 (called to the bar, Inner Temple, 1976) but practiced law for 17 years before being elevated to judge in 1992. His career milestones (Chief Justice Peshawar High Court 2004, Chief Justice of Pakistan 2014, caretaker PM 2018) all came decades later.
early_history_summary: Born into a wealthy, politically influential Pashtun family in Swat, Mulk earned his LLB from Peshawar University in 1972 and was called to the bar at Inner Temple London in 1976. He then practiced law at Peshawar High Court for over 17 years before his elevation to the bench.
family_context_summary: Born into a wealthy and politically influential Mitravi Swati Pashtun family in Swat; his father Kamran Khan was a businessman and senator (1973-1977), and his brother Shuja-ul-Mulk also served as senator.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a politician/senator and businessman; family had political influence in Swat region, but no direct legal domain transfer documented.

name: Ana Beatriz Barros
milestone_by_age_26: Placed second worldwide in the 1996 Elite Model Look competition at age 14, launching an international modeling career that included the GUESS Millennium campaign and Victoria's Secret and Sports Illustrated Swimsuit appearances by age 20.
early_history_summary: Spotted at age 13 while vacationing in Rio de Janeiro with her sister, Barros entered the 1996 Elite Model Look and placed second worldwide. Elite sent her portfolio to GUESS, leading to the Millennium campaign alongside Alessandra Ambrosio, and she subsequently appeared in Victoria's Secret shows and Sports Illustrated Swimsuit editions from 2002 onward.
family_context_summary: Born to a middle-class family in Itabira, Minas Gerais; father Reinato Barros was a mechanical engineer, mother Sônia was a housewife. Family moved to Rio de Janeiro during her childhood.
primary_early_advantage_tags: physical attributes, elite agency pipeline, sibling model, Rio fashion market
evidence_summary: Barros was discovered at 13 and placed second worldwide in the 1996 Elite Model Look, which directly led to the GUESS Millennium campaign and subsequent Victoria's Secret and Sports Illustrated work by age 20. Her exceptional physical attributes (5'11", green eyes, distinctive look) were the primary catalyst, amplified by Elite Model Management's pipeline. Her older sister Patricia was also spotted and modeled, providing a peer companion in the industry. Family was middle-class with no prior fashion industry connections.
starting_point: Born to a middle-class family in Itabira, Minas Gerais, Brazil; father was a mechanical engineer, mother a housewife; family later moved to Rio de Janeiro where she was spotted at age 13.
current_position: Brazilian model known for Victoria's Secret and Sports Illustrated work; married to Karim El Chiaty since 2016; mother of two; continues modeling selectively.

trajectory.event: Placed second worldwide in the Elite Model Look competition, launching her professional modeling career.
Featured in the GUESS Millennium campaign alongside Alessandra Ambrosio, gaining international exposure.
Appeared in Victoria's Secret Fashion Show and Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue, establishing herself as a top model.
Continued appearances in Sports Illustrated Swimsuit editions and major fashion campaigns through the mid-2000s.
Married Karim El Chiaty and shifted to selective modeling work while raising a family.

name: Roberto Cavalli
milestone_by_age_26: No specific dated material milestone by age 26 found. While a student at the Florence Academy of Art (enrolled 1957), he made flower prints on knit that attracted hosiery manufacturers, but no specific date is documented. His first dated collection debuted in Paris in 1970 at age 30, and his first namesake collection was presented at age 32.
early_history_summary: Cavalli enrolled at the Academy of Art in Florence in 1957, experimenting with textile printing techniques. While still a student he created flower prints on knitwear that caught the attention of Italian hosiery manufacturers, though the specific date is undocumented. His breakthrough came in 1970 when he invented and patented a leather printing process and debuted in Paris.
family_context_summary: Born in a suburb of Florence; grandfather Giuseppe Rossi was an Impressionist painter whose work was exhibited in the Uffizi Gallery; mother was a seamstress. Father was killed in 1944 in the Cavriglia massacre when Cavalli was four.
parent_family_domain_summary: Grandfather was a celebrated Impressionist painter and mother was a seamstress, providing artistic and textile heritage, though no direct evidence of early career transfer is documented.

name: Luis Medina Cantalejo
milestone_by_age_26: Reached the Primera División (top Spanish football league) as a referee in 1988 at age 24, officiating 155 top-flight matches over his career.
early_history_summary: Medina Cantalejo began refereeing at age 18 in 1982 and rapidly ascended through the Spanish football pyramid, reaching the Primera División by 1988 at age 24. He became an international referee in 2002 and went on to officiate at the 2006 FIFA World Cup and the 2009 UEFA Cup final.
family_context_summary: Born in Tomares, Sevilla, Spain. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Spanish football federation referee pipeline, La Liga, Seville football culture
evidence_summary: Medina Cantalejo started refereeing at 18 and reached Spain's Primera División by 24, a rapid ascent through the Spanish football referee pipeline. Growing up in Seville, a major Spanish football city, provided direct domain exposure. No family background or financial advantages are documented in reviewed sources. His career trajectory was driven by early specialization and the Spanish football federation's referee development system.

current_position: President of the Comité Técnico de Árbitros (CTA) of the RFEF and Vocal of the Royal Spanish Football Federation since January 2022; retired from active refereeing in 2009.

name: Vladislav Volkov
milestone_by_age_26: Served as acting deputy lead designer of the Vostok spacecraft at Korolev's OKB-1 design bureau from September 1961 at age 25, directly contributing to the Soviet manned spaceflight program.
early_history_summary: Volkov graduated from the Moscow Aviation Institute in 1959 and joined OKB-1 (Korolev's design bureau) as an engineer. He worked on the R-9A ICBM and Voskhod launch vehicle, and by September 1961 was serving as acting deputy lead designer for the Vostok spacecraft, the vessel that carried cosmonauts into orbit. He was selected as a cosmonaut in 1966 and flew on Soyuz 7 (1969) and Soyuz 11 (1971).
family_context_summary: Born in Moscow, Soviet Union. Family background not well documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Moscow Aviation Institute, Korolev OKB-1, Soviet space program, Vostok spacecraft
evidence_summary: Volkov graduated from the prestigious Moscow Aviation Institute in 1959 and immediately joined OKB-1, the Korolev Design Bureau at the heart of the Soviet space program. By age 25 he was acting deputy lead designer for the Vostok spacecraft, a remarkable position of responsibility for someone so young, working at the frontier of human spaceflight during the Space Race. His trajectory was defined by deep immersion in the Soviet aerospace engineering ecosystem. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in Moscow, Soviet Union; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died on June 30, 1971 at age 35 during the Soyuz 11 reentry accident; final role: flight engineer of Soyuz 11 and crew member of the world's first space station (Salyut 1).

trajectory.event: Graduated from Moscow Aviation Institute and joined OKB-1 (Korolev Design Bureau) as an engineer.
Appointed acting deputy lead designer of the Vostok spacecraft at OKB-1.
Selected as a cosmonaut in the civilian specialist group.
Flew on Soyuz 7 as flight engineer in the first group flight of three spacecraft; awarded Hero of the Soviet Union.
Flew on Soyuz 11 to Salyut 1, the first space station mission; died during reentry due to decompression accident.

name: Semmy Schilt
milestone_by_age_26: Became the Openweight King of Pancrase on November 28, 1999 at age 26, defeating Yuki Kondo via rear naked choke to claim the MMA title.
early_history_summary: Schilt began practicing Kyokushin karate at age 8, following his parents who were both recreational practitioners. He switched to Ashihara karate at 12 and earned his black belt at 18. He debuted in professional MMA with Pancrase in May 1996 at age 22 and won the King of Pancrase title in November 1999 at age 26, later transitioning to kickboxing where he won four K-1 World Grand Prix titles.
family_context_summary: Born in Rotterdam, Netherlands; both parents practiced martial arts recreationally. Father owned a transport company. Schilt trained in mechanical engineering before pursuing fighting full-time.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents practiced Kyokushin karate recreationally, introducing Schilt to martial arts at age 8, though not at a competitive or professional level.
primary_early_advantage_tags: exceptional height 212cm, parental martial arts introduction, Dutch kickboxing tradition, early karate training
evidence_summary: Schilt's extraordinary physical stature (212cm, ~130kg) combined with early martial arts training from age 8, introduced by his recreational-practitioner parents, created a unique competitive advantage. The Netherlands has a strong kickboxing tradition, providing a fertile training ecosystem. He earned his black belt at 18 and transitioned to professional MMA at 22, winning the King of Pancrase title at 26. His father's transport company provided some flexibility for training. His physical edge was the dominant factor in his combat sports career.
starting_point: Born in Rotterdam, Netherlands; both parents practiced martial arts recreationally; father owned a transport company; grew up with early exposure to karate.
current_position: Retired professional kickboxer and MMA fighter; runs Fight Game Academy; widely regarded as the greatest heavyweight kickboxer of all time with four K-1 World GP titles and one Glory Grand Slam title.

trajectory.event: Earned black belt in Ashihara karate at age 18.

name: Rineke Dijkstra
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Her first solo exhibition at Gallery de Moor in Amsterdam in 1984 (age 25) was a minor gallery debut. Her artistic breakthrough came with the Beach Portraits series starting in 1992 (age 33), and major recognition followed with the Citibank Prize in 1999 and Hasselblad Award in 2017.
early_history_summary: Dijkstra studied photography at the Gerrit Rietveld Academie in Amsterdam from 1981 to 1986, then worked commercially taking corporate portraits and annual report photos. Her first solo exhibition was in 1984 at Gallery de Moor in Amsterdam. Her artistic awakening came with a 1991 self-portrait, leading to the Beach Portraits series that made her reputation.
family_context_summary: Born in Sittard, Netherlands. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.

name: Erich Kühnhackl
milestone_by_age_26: Won the German Championship with EV Landshut in 1970 at age 19, scoring 21 goals in 35 games in his second Bundesliga season, and later won an Olympic bronze medal at the 1976 Winter Olympics at age 25.
early_history_summary: Kühnhackl grew up in Czechoslovakia where he began playing hockey, emigrating to West Germany in 1968 at age 18 after the Soviet invasion. He joined EV Landshut and in his second season (1969-70) won the German Championship as a 19-year-old. He went on to become the greatest German hockey player of the 20th century, winning four German championships, an Olympic bronze in 1976, and leading the Bundesliga in scoring eight times.
family_context_summary: Born in Citice, Czechoslovakia to a family of German descent; family emigrated to West Germany in 1968 after the Soviet occupation. Family background beyond this not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources, though the family's German heritage in Czechoslovakia and subsequent emigration suggest a displaced background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: exceptional size 6'5" 213lbs, Czech hockey tradition, EV Landshut, coach Karel Gut, displacement from Czechoslovakia
evidence_summary: Kühnhackl's exceptional physical size (6'5", 213 lbs) was extraordinary for hockey in his era and gave him a dominant edge. Growing up in Czechoslovakia, where hockey was the national sport, provided deep early immersion. After emigrating to West Germany at 18 following the Soviet invasion, he joined EV Landshut where coach Karel Gut accelerated his development. He won the German Championship at 19 and Olympic bronze at 25. The displacement from Czechoslovakia created both adversity and opportunity, catalyzing his professional career in Germany.
starting_point: Born in Citice, Czechoslovakia to a family of German descent; family emigrated to West Germany in 1968 after the Soviet invasion, settling in Landshut.
current_position: Retired German ice hockey legend; named German ice hockey player of the century in 2000; IIHF Hall of Fame inductee (1997); former vice president of the German Ice Hockey Federation (2010-2014).

trajectory.event: Emigrated from Czechoslovakia to West Germany and joined EV Landshut.

name: Toto Cutugno
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. He founded his first band at 19 (1962) and played drums in various groups through the 1960s, but his songwriting career began in the early 1970s (age 27+) and his first Sanremo appearance with Albatros was in 1976 (age 33). His worldwide hit 'L'Italiano' came in 1983 and Eurovision win in 1990.
early_history_summary: Cutugno began his musical career as a drummer, founding his first band Toto e i Tati at 19. He played in various groups through the 1960s before forming the disco band Albatros and starting a songwriting career in the early 1970s, composing hits for Joe Dassin, Dalida, and others. His solo breakthrough came with winning Sanremo in 1980 and the worldwide hit 'L'Italiano' in 1983.
family_context_summary: Born in Fosdinovo, Tuscany to a Sicilian sea marshal father who played trumpet, and a Tuscan housewife mother. Family moved to La Spezia shortly after his birth. Father encouraged him to play drums self-taught.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a sea marshal and amateur trumpet player who encouraged Cutugno's early musical interest, but no professional music industry transfer is documented.

name: Chris Slade
milestone_by_age_26: Played drums on Tom Jones's hit single 'It's Not Unusual' in 1965 at age 19, and later became a founding member of Manfred Mann's Earth Band in 1971 at age 25, recording eight albums with the group.
early_history_summary: Slade grew up in Pontypridd, Wales, the same area as Tom Jones, and played drums in Jones's backing band The Squires for seven years starting in the early 1960s. He played on Jones's 1965 hit 'It's Not Unusual' at age 19. After leaving Tom Jones in 1969, he became a founding member of Manfred Mann's Earth Band in 1971, recording eight albums and achieving UK Top Ten singles including the US #1 'Blinded by the Light.'
family_context_summary: Born Christopher Slade Rees in Pontypridd, Glamorgan, South Wales. From the same area as Tom Jones. Family background not well documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Tom Jones backing band, Welsh music scene, 1960s British pop wave, Manfred Mann's Earth Band
evidence_summary: Slade's early career was catalyzed by geographic proximity to Tom Jones in Pontypridd, Wales, joining Jones's backing band The Squires as a teenager and playing on the 1965 hit 'It's Not Unusual' at age 19. The 1960s British pop music wave provided a structural tailwind. His seven-year tenure with Tom Jones provided professional reps and industry exposure, leading to his founding role in Manfred Mann's Earth Band at 25. No family financial or domain advantages are documented.
starting_point: Born in Pontypridd, Glamorgan, South Wales; from the same area as Tom Jones; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Welsh rock drummer; returned to AC/DC in 2015 for the Rock or Bust World Tour; continues to perform actively after a 60-year career spanning Tom Jones, Manfred Mann's Earth Band, Uriah Heep, The Firm, and AC/DC.

name: Okko Kamu
milestone_by_age_26: Won first prize at the inaugural Herbert von Karajan Conducting Competition in Berlin in 1969 at age 23, launching his international conducting career, and became principal conductor of the Finnish Radio Symphony Orchestra in 1971 at age 25.
early_history_summary: Kamu was born into a musical family in Helsinki; his father played double bass in the Helsinki Philharmonic and his mother was a violin maker. He began violin studies at age two, entered the Sibelius Academy at six, and became concertmaster of the Finnish National Opera orchestra at 20. Self-taught as a conductor, he won the Karajan Competition in 1969 at 23 and became principal conductor of the Finnish Radio Symphony Orchestra at 25.
family_context_summary: Born in Helsinki; son of Adam Kamu, a double bass player in the Helsinki Philharmonic, and Eine (Syrjänen) Kamu, a violin maker. Grew up immersed in orchestral music from birth.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a professional musician in the Helsinki Philharmonic, providing direct domain immersion and access to the orchestra from childhood. Mother was a violin maker, further embedding the family in music culture.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father Helsinki Philharmonic musician, violin from age 2, Sibelius Academy at 6, Finnish National Opera, Karajan Competition
evidence_summary: Kamu's extraordinary early musical development was driven by deep family-domain immersion: his father played double bass in the Helsinki Philharmonic and his mother was a violin maker. He began violin at age two, entered the Sibelius Academy at six, and was sitting in on Philharmonic rehearsals as a child. He became concertmaster of the Finnish National Opera at 20 and, self-taught as a conductor, won the Karajan Competition at 23. His trajectory was defined by the family-domain apprenticeship archetype, with the Finnish musical elite pipeline providing institutional acceleration.
starting_point: Born in Helsinki, Finland; son of Adam Kamu, a double bass player in the Helsinki Philharmonic Orchestra, and Eine Kamu, a violin maker; grew up immersed in classical music from birth.
current_position: Finnish conductor; principal conductor of the Lahti Symphony Orchestra since 2011; continues to conduct internationally with major orchestras; has led the Finnish Radio Symphony Orchestra, Oslo Philharmonic, and Helsinki Philharmonic.

name: Zhu Ting
milestone_by_age_26: Won MVP, Best Scorer, and Best Spiker at the 2013 FIVB U20 World Championship at age 18, leading China to the title without losing a set, and later won Olympic gold and MVP at the 2016 Rio Olympics at age 21.
early_history_summary: Zhu Ting grew up in a rural farming family in Henan province, China, and started volleyball at age 13 when a teacher recommended her to a sports school. She joined the Chinese youth national team at 15, won her first MVP at the 2012 Asian Junior Championship at 17, and dominated the 2013 FIVB U20 World Championship at 18. She was handpicked for the senior national team by legendary coach Lang Ping in 2013 and won Olympic gold and MVP at Rio 2016 at age 21.
family_context_summary: Born to a farming family in Zhudalou village, Henan province; third of five children; family was in debt (over 100,000 yuan) and Zhu nearly left school to work in a factory before a teacher recommended sports school. Parents took extra part-time jobs to fund three years of training (costing ~126,000 yuan).
parent_family_domain_summary: No volleyball or sports domain background in the family; parents were farmers with no athletic heritage documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Chinese national volleyball pipeline, Lang Ping coaching, exceptional height 1.98m, rural poverty catalyst, sports school system
evidence_summary: Zhu Ting's rise from rural poverty to volleyball superstardom was driven by her exceptional physical attributes (1.98m tall), the Chinese national team sports pipeline that identified her at 15, and the mentorship of legendary coach Lang Ping. Her farming family's financial hardship (debt of 100,000+ yuan) created urgency and a distinctive motivation, with her parents sacrificing to fund her training. The Chinese sports school system provided the institutional pipeline that transformed her raw physical talent into elite skill. By 18 she was U20 World Champion and MVP; by 21 she was Olympic champion and MVP.
starting_point: Born to a farming family in Zhudalou village, Henan province, China; third of five children; family was in debt and she nearly left school to work in a factory before a teacher recommended her to a sports school at age 13.
current_position: Chinese volleyball superstar; plays for Imoco Volley Conegliano; Olympic gold medalist and MVP (Rio 2016); two-time FIVB World Cup MVP; widely regarded as one of the greatest volleyball players of all time; member of China's National People's Congress.

trajectory.event: Selected for the Chinese youth national volleyball team.
